requirements.requirement: Persistently disable IPv4 ICMP redirect acceptance (accept_redirects) on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed accept_redirects=1 for all/default (cmd-973ffdbb47ae42c8). Ansible playbook using ansible.posix.sysctl set both to 0 and persisted to /etc/sysctl.d/60-disable-icmp-redirects-source-route.conf (cmd-3bad7819a6ed4431, cmd-e53715fa80024429), confirmed at runtime and in the persisted file immediately after (cmd-edae732de90e4432), and after a full node1 reboot (boot_id bdd5de93->6b6cbb9d) both runtime sysctl values and the persisted file still show 0 (cmd-9ea42a58db714448, cmd-66621d15ca724222, cmd-7f2569f50b2e44e1), directly demonstrating survival across a genuine restart.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable IPv4 source-routed packet acceptance (accept_source_route) on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed accept_source_route inconsistent (0 for all, 1 for default) (cmd-973ffdbb47ae42c8). The same playbook run set both all/default to 0, persisted to /etc/sysctl.d/60-disable-icmp-redirects-source-route.conf, verified at runtime and in the file (cmd-e53715fa80024429, cmd-edae732de90e4432), and confirmed unchanged (still 0) after node1's reboot (cmd-7f2569f50b2e44e1) and again via an ansible ad-hoc re-check from node2 (cmd-91081dd0ea6243d2).

An Ansible inventory and playbook (harden.yml, ansible.posix.sysctl module, sysctl_set + sysctl_file) were authored on control node2 (cmd-c0605a81541b4b78, cmd-3bad7819a6ed4431) and run against node1 via ansible-playbook, reporting all four sysctl tasks changed with no failures (cmd-e53715fa80024429). Necessary SSH connectivity from node2 to node1 (host-key generation, sshd start, authorized_keys, /etc/hosts entry) was established beforehand to make this possible (cmd-4efebdeeefe94025, cmd-13797c4336ec4ab2, cmd-618d5cfa34f84915, cmd-8a5e47e05f4448a9).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on all managed nodes (node1, node2)
requirements.summary: For node1: pre-restart healthy baseline with boot_id bdd5de93 and hardened sysctl/file state (cmd-9ea42a58db714448), reboot acknowledgement and unreachability window (cmd-66621d15ca724222, cmd-d97bb2ca6c774f37, cmd-f50314d473034b31, cmd-cd0f97d9a6484463), and recovered state with new boot_id 6b6cbb9d and intact hardening (cmd-7f2569f50b2e44e1) -- corroborated by the fixed lifecycle before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots. For node2: pre-restart baseline boot_id eefaca89 (cmd-2a50d96a0e0440a2), reboot acknowledgement/unreachability (cmd-1ed80d1a13de4d9f, cmd-2087134991954ed9, cmd-1613447df90847a5, cmd-d2bdfb03dcf34b36), and recovered state with new boot_id 1ad04081, functioning Ansible, and a successful ad-hoc re-verification against node1 (cmd-91081dd0ea6243d2).

overall_summary: The executor used Ansible from control node2 (ansible.posix.sysctl) to persistently disable IPv4 ICMP redirect and source-route acceptance on node1, with baseline, applied, and post-reboot verification all directly evidenced -- a strong demonstration of persistence across an actual reboot. Prerequisite SSH-enablement mutations on node1 were necessary and bounded, and the separate provider-wide restart-evidence protocol was completed cleanly for both node1 and node2 with matching boot-identity, service, and hardening state before and after.
limitations: Reliance is placed on the executor-reported command IDs and captured stdout; no independent tool access was available to re-run verification.

The lifecycle after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare was disabled), so preparer-vs-executor separation relies solely on the executor timeline rather than an independent prepare-phase snapshot.

operational_hygiene.summary: Every state-changing command traces to a legitimate purpose: enabling SSH-based Ansible management of node1 (ssh-keygen -A + systemctl start ssh in cmd-4efebdeeefe94025, since node1 shipped with no host keys and a failed ssh.service; adding node2's pubkey to node1's authorized_keys in cmd-13797c4336ec4ab2; appending node1 to node2's /etc/hosts in cmd-618d5cfa34f84915), applying the required sysctl hardening (cmd-e53715fa80024429), and the two node reboots (node1: cmd-66621d15ca724222; node2: cmd-1ed80d1a13de4d9f) performed to generate restart evidence, both of which completed cleanly with services and hardening intact afterward. The earlier failed ssh start attempt (cmd-c214085746154278) was a diagnostic step preceding the actual fix, not a persisted mutation. No abandoned files, failed services, or unnecessary/broad mutations remain in the after_executor snapshot. The persistent addition of node2's root SSH key to node1's authorized_keys is a necessary and expected artifact of the control_node topology rather than unwanted residue.
